resolutions.researcher_notes: Live opec.org original 301s to the homepage (confirmed dead, known gotcha) but the Wayback snapshot resolves; pdftotext -f 78 -l 78 of that snapshot recovers Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011' (p.75 of doc), Libya section, row 'Khoms/Tripoli Sirte Oil 125 34 17,048,995 na' -- listing the line as an active OPEC-member gas pipeline transporting a stated volume in 2011 (status inferred from context per rule 4, not a literal token; url_verifier's substring miss on 'Khoms' is expected/known for this ligature-heavy PDF and is a screen artifact, manually confirmed). Independently, Libya Monitor (live, verified) lists a tender titled 'Maintenance of Khoms-Tripoli gas pipeline' closing 8 Feb 2022 -- a maintenance contract on an in-service line 11 years later, from a wholly separate origin (a project-tenders database, not OPEC/GEM-adjacent). Two independent sources, ~decade apart, both consistent with continuous operating status; no source found suggesting shelving/decommissioning.

OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 (Wayback-recovered, pdftotext-confirmed) lists the Khoms/Tripoli line under the section header 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011'. Independently, ognnews.com's project report on the Khoms-Tripoli line describes it as delivering 'feedstock to Khoms gas-fired power plant' (i.e. natural gas). Two independent origins agree the commodity is gas.

OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 (Wayback snapshot of the dead opec.org PDF, pdftotext -f 78 -l 78) lists row 'Khoms/Tripoli Sirte Oil 125 34 17,048,995 na' under a capacity column headed '(1,000 scm/yr)'. 17,048,995 thousand scm/yr = 17.048995 bcm/yr, an exact match to the sheet's Capacity=17.05 bcm/y. Treated as high per the confidence-tiers rubric's 'one primary/regulatory source' allowance (OPEC's own statistical bulletin). FLAG: a wholly separate, later Khoms-Tripoli project -- a NEW pipeline built to feed the Khoms power plant, per ognnews.com (2005, EPC retendering, ~160km/34-24in) and the seed alwasat.com article (~2010, Punj Lloyd India contract, 126km+32km branch, 106 MMcf/d/~1.1 bcm/y) -- carries very different specs from the sheet's values. The sheet's exact 17.05/201/34 triple matches only the older Sirte-Oil-operated line in OPEC's table, not the newer completion project the seed citation actually describes; flagging this as a probable two-different-vintages-of-the-same-named-corridor situation rather than a single contradiction to resolve.

Same OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 row: 'Khoms/Tripoli ... 125 [miles] 34 [in] 17,048,995 [1,000 scm/yr]'. 125 miles = 201.17 km, matching the sheet's LengthKnown=201.00 km almost exactly. High per the primary/regulatory-source allowance. FLAG (same as Capacity): ognnews.com's Khoms-Tripoli project report gives a different, newer-project length of ~160 km, and the seed alwasat article gives 126 km + 32 km of branches (~158 km) for the Punj Lloyd completion project -- neither matches 201 km. As with Capacity, the sheet value lines up with the OPEC-listed older Sirte Oil line, not the newer completion project the seed citation covers; treated as two distinct historical builds of a same-named corridor rather than forcing a single reconciled number.

OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 lists diameter=34 inches for Khoms/Tripoli/Sirte Oil, an exact match. Independently, ognnews.com's report on the (separate, newer) Khoms-Tripoli project also specifies '34-inch and 24-inch' pipe -- the 34in figure recurs across both the older operating line and the newer completion project, so both sources agree on 34in even though they otherwise describe different-vintage builds (see Capacity/Length notes).

The mainsheet's FuelSource field holds this Al Wasat (Bahrain) URL as its literal 'value' -- an ingestion quirk (a citation link stored in a data cell rather than a fuel-source name), same pattern seen on other Libya rows in this batch. Verified live (200, not gem.wiki/blocklisted) and on-topic: the article ('Punj Lloyd India wins contract to execute the Tripoli-Mellitah gas pipeline project in Libya') explicitly covers the Khoms-Tripoli line by name too, reporting it at 126 km plus 32 km of branch lines, designed for 106 MMcf/d, contracted to Punj Lloyd (India), signed by Sirte Oil & Gas Co. board chair Ahmad Aoun. Re-affirmed as a legitimate, verifiable reference (satisfies standing rule 3) rather than replaced. FLAG: this article describes the newer Khoms-Tripoli completion project (~2010, different length/capacity than the OPEC-table line used for Capacity/Length above) -- see those units' notes for the two-vintages issue; the URL itself remains a valid, on-topic citation regardless.

OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 names the segment 'Khoms/Tripoli' directly, matching StartLocation=Khoms/EndLocation=Tripoli. ognnews.com independently names the same route ('Khoms-Tripoli') and adds that it delivers gas to the Khoms power plant, i.e. Khoms as the western/producing end and Tripoli as the route's other terminus. Both Khoms (seat of Murqub district) and Tripoli (capital, Tripoli district), Libya, are uncontested, well-known place identifications; no source conflicts on the two endpoints.

OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 names 'Sirte Oil' as the owner/operator of the Khoms/Tripoli segment specifically. ognnews.com's project report states the client is 'Sirte Oil Company (subsidiary of National Oil Corporation)' explicitly. Independently, Wikipedia's Sirte Oil Company article states SOC is 'an oil and gas company in Libya operating under the state-owned National Oil Corporation (NOC)'. Two independent sources (a trade project-report and an encyclopedia entry, tracing to different origins) agree Sirte Oil Co. is wholly under NOC, supporting Owner1=Libyan National Oil Corp at 100% via its subsidiary; neither source gives an explicit ownership percentage for SOC itself, but both describe it as state-owned/NOC-controlled with no other named shareholder, consistent with the sheet's 100% figure.
